hints: Focus on two separate ideas here, counting total electrons for a charged ion and comparing molecular shapes using VSEPR theory.
Add up the electrons from one N (7) plus four H (4 x 1) then subtract one for the 1+ charge to get the total for $\text{NH}_4^+$.
Think how the lone pair on $\text{NH}_3$ squeezes the bond angle, and what happens to that squeezing when the lone pair becomes a fourth N-H bond.
walkthrough:
**Count electrons in the ammonium ion**

Think of electrons as simple addition, then adjust for charge. Nitrogen brings 7, each hydrogen brings 1.

$$\text{total for } \text{NH}_4^+ = 7 + (4 \times 1) - 1 = 10$$

**Draw the shapes of ammonia and ammonium**

Ammonia, $\text{NH}_3$, has 3 bond pairs plus 1 lone pair on N, so it is trigonal pyramidal. Ammonium forms by dative bonding to $\text{H}^+$:
$$\text{NH}_3 + \text{H}^+ \rightarrow \text{NH}_4^+$$
Now N has 4 bond pairs and no lone pair, so it is tetrahedral.

**Decide what happens to the H-N-H angle**

In $\text{NH}_3$, the lone pair repels more strongly and squeezes the angle down to about $107^{\circ}$. In $\text{NH}_4^+$, with four equal bond pairs, the angle opens to the perfect tetrahedral $109.5^{\circ}$. So the angle increases, giving 10 electrons and an increase.

options.A: Incorrect. 8 is the number of valence electrons around N, not the total electrons in the ion. The angle also does not decrease, it opens up when the lone pair is removed.
options.B: Incorrect. The angle change is correct (increases), but 8 is wrong. Students who count only outer shell electrons or forget the inner 1s electrons on N get 8 instead of the full total of 10.
options.C: Incorrect. 10 electrons is correct, but the angle does not decrease. This trap comes from thinking more H atoms means more crowding, whereas VSEPR shows loss of the lone pair actually reduces repulsion.
options.D: Correct. Total electrons = 7 + 4 - 1 = 10, and shape changes from pyramidal ($107^{\circ}$) to tetrahedral ($109.5^{\circ}$), so the H-N-H angle increases.
